To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transforming Src mutant Src(E378G), like v-Src, stimulates the shedding of TGFalpha via activation of ADAM 17.
a transforming Src mutant increases bioavailability of EGFG ligands via activation of ADAM 17, which can lead to autocrine and paracrinesignaling via the EGFR.
a transforming mutant of Src, the Src(E378G mutant, increases the bioavailability (i.e., shedding and release) of EGFR ligand via stimulation of the metalloproteinase Adam17.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a potential mechanism by which oncogenic tyrosin kinases can promote tumorigenesis via activation of ADAM metalloproteinases.
the role of Src-mediated activation of ADAM proteases in promoting tumorigenicity and metastasis.
the regulation of ADAM17, a cell surface metalloprotease that regulates signaling of the epidermal-growth-factor-receptor and is implicated in cancer and rheumatological diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transforming mutant Src(E378G), but not the wild type Src, can stimulate the shedding of TGF-α by activating the cell surface metalloproteinase, ADAM17, and that Src(E378G)/ADAM17-mediated release of TGF- α from the cell surface can lead to enhanced paracine EGFR/ERK signaling.
Src activation can stimulate ADAM17 to shed TGFα, and that the shed TGFα can then activate the EGFR and downstream signaling pathways in an autocrine or paracrine fashion.
ADAM17 can mediate the release of EGFR-activating ligands from the surface of Src-expressing cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADAM17 can mediate EGFR signaling in a paracrine fashion, which may be relevant for cancer progression.
ADAM17 can mediate EGFR activation in a Src-dependent manner, and this could be a potential therapeutic target in Src-dependent tumors.

oncogenic forms of the Src tyrosine kinase stimulate ADAM17-mediated release of EGFR-ligands, which in turn can activate EGFR and ERKS signaling in an autocrine manner in Src-transformed tumor cells as well as in a paracrine manner in surrounding non-transforming stromal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Src can stimulate ADAM17 to release TGFα, which can then activate ERK signaling.
Src can stimulate the shedding of EGFR ligand via ADAM17 and that this process is important for Src-mediated activation of ERK signaling.
Src can enhance EGFR signaling via ADAM17-mediated release of EGFR-ligands, which can be important in promoting tumorigenicity and metastasis.
